questions.question: How many crew quarters are in the module?
What did he compare the size of a crew quarter to?
Why is the sleeping bag fixed to the wall?
questions.expected: So he doesn't float away or kick anything.

questions.question: What were the two computers used for?
questions.expected: One for the schedule, official emails and procedures; the other for internet access, which he tweets from.

questions.question: What does he use the headset for?
questions.expected: Personal calls to the ground, to talk with family and friends after hours and on weekends.

questions.question: What does he watch on the iPad?
questions.expected: Movies and news programmes that the ground uplinks.

questions.question: Where are Sergey and Misha's crew quarters?
What did the sign above the hatch say?
questions.expected: EXIT (a label there also read OVHD).

questions.question: Which space agency's name appeared on a patch?
What was the man giving the tour wearing?
What happened right after he talked about the telephone box?
questions.expected: He said he had slept in that same place on his first long-duration flight four years earlier, then showed how to get in and described the sleeping bag.

questions.question: Which did he show first, the computers or the sleeping bag?
What was the tour about, overall?
questions.expected: The crew quarters of a spacecraft: where he sleeps, and the computers and equipment he uses to work and stay in touch.

questions.question: When he mentioned tweeting, what was he showing?
questions.expected: His two computers; he tweets from the one with internet access.

questions.question: Who did I have lunch with?
What did he say about the food on board?
What is the name of the man who gave the tour?
What did I do on Monday morning?
